purpose: LLM comparison for content creation, SEO, and site development tasks

tasks.description: Generating JSON-LD, optimizing meta tags for CTR, and ensuring site-wide technical SEO health.

recommendation.reason: Best precision for large HTML files, consistent tone control, and accurate on-page SEO edits (titles, metas, H1s, scannability) without hallucinating facts. Excellent at emotional yet honest CTR-focused titles and meta descriptions.
recommendation.notes: Use Grok for fast title/meta brainstorming, prompt refinement, and real-time GSC-based strategy. Claude wins for bulk editing of your 175+ pages.

tasks.description: Writing the core 'Book vs. Movie' analysis. High focus on 'vibe,' emotional honesty, and spoiler-heavy depth.

recommendation.reason: Superior at long-form, balanced, honest prose. It naturally delivers the 'no sugarcoating' tone you want while maintaining factual accuracy and strong narrative flow.
recommendation.notes: Use Grok when you need sharper, more direct opinions or timely angles tied to current trends and your existing GSC data (e.g., Colleen Hoover pages).

tasks.description: Transforming raw research into your specific .json format for the site injection pipeline.

recommendation.reason: Extremely reliable at following complex schemas and producing clean, consistent JSON output. Handles your structured comparison format very well.
recommendation.notes: Grok is fast for smaller batches and debugging schema issues in conversation. For true high-volume bulk processing, DeepSeek or Claude would be more cost-efficient.

tasks.description: Finding upcoming 2026/2027 adaptations, casting rumors, and tracking viral 'book-tok' trends.

recommendation.reason: Strong real-time awareness and ability to connect trends directly to your current GSC performance (mobile clicks, review snippets, striking-distance queries). Good at practical, actionable strategy tied to your specific site data.
recommendation.notes: Use Grok for holistic strategy that considers your early traffic patterns and content pipeline. Perplexity is better for pure fact-checking of release dates.

tasks.description: Designing 'shelves,' hero sections, and alphabetized browse components in the Astro environment.

recommendation.reason: Best at clean, production-ready HTML/CSS refactoring while perfectly preserving your existing classes, schema, and simple design style.
recommendation.notes: Grok is excellent for rapid prototyping and live iteration (as we did with the welcome page and A Beautiful Mind edits). Use Grok when you want quick feedback loops in chat.

general_guidelines.tone: Honest, spoiler-heavy, no sugarcoating, opinionated but factual
general_guidelines.site_strength: Deep, high-quality individual comparison pages with strong structured data and clear verdicts
general_guidelines.current_focus: Improving CTR on existing impressions, making the homepage more welcoming and curated, and scaling efficiently with 175+ pages
general_guidelines.recommended_workflow: Grok (strategy + quick tests) → Claude 4 Sonnet (heavy writing, SEO editing, HTML refactoring) → DeepSeek (if doing true high-volume bulk JSON work)
